title: Gen-CA
fill_note: DENSE layered wind with a jig; scorer cap 0.65
fill_how: The scored turns assume a dense, layer-by-layer wind at fill 0.65 (insulated-wire area / window; the scorer cap). Use a winding jig on a drill/lathe with a turn counter, lay each layer side-by-side with light back-tension, and do not scramble-wind: a scramble wind only reaches ≈0.55–0.60 and then the window holds fewer turns (scorer what-if `--fill 0.60` is in the table above). Never wind more than the listed turns — the copper must stay below the flanges.
steel_extra: **New steel:** Ø194 discs, M3 clamp map R30 at 0/90/180/270° and R44 on the inter-pole angles 67.5/112.5/247.5/292.5° (both inside the R84 magnet ring). Cut from this kit's `steel_backiron_disc.dxf`; no earlier disc fits.
o5_note: scan t6: diametric Ø5 assists lower this 8p/12c layout, so all 48 Ø5 are left out
card_title: Gen-CA · dual-rotor 8p/12c R84 · segmented magnet arcs + annular stator (nested one-plate)
card_sub: 12 bobbins r64–104 × 4.95 mm copper (gap 7.55 mm) · poles R84 · 16 arcs on 2× Ø194 steel · bases print in place · no Ø5 · 2026-10-13
idea: Break the plate limit instead of the physics: the 2026-10-11 scans showed watts keep rising with machine size, but Ø194 was the largest one-piece stator/rotor set that fits one 410 mm plate. Gen-CA makes the steel disc the structural rotor and prints the magnet carrier as 8 bolt-on arcs per rotor plus a separate D-flat hub, opens the stator centre, and prints the 12 bobbin bases in place inside their stator bays, so a much bigger R84 / Ø226 machine (bobbins r64–104, 4.95 mm copper, 7.55 mm magnet gap) still packs on ONE plate.
halb_block:
halbach_magnetisation = "none";  // NO O5 assist magnets in this kit (scan: they lower the 4-pole score)
rotor_b_same_axis   = true;     // same-index magnets share one axis: N faces S across the gap
